deadline.value: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis with deadlines 3 months prior to the intended start date for international applicants (30 June for September start).
deadline.quote: 3 months prior to the intended start date (for international applicants) or 2 months prior to the intended start date (for home applicants). For example, for an end of September start, the deadline is 30 June (international) and 31 July (home).

entry_route.value: A first-class or upper second-class UK Honours degree (or equivalent), or a relevant Master's degree.
entry_route.quote: A first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent)

supervisor.value: Applicants are encouraged to consult staff research profiles to identify potential supervisors in their project area.
supervisor.quote: Use the University website to find specific staff who might be able to supervise in your project area.

funding.value: Funding is competitive via university research studentships, research councils, or project-specific funding.
funding.quote: You will register for the PhD for four years but, if you are awarded a studentship, funding may only cover a period of three or three-and-a-half years. Most students are able to complete within this time, and, subject to approval by the University, fees may be reduced for a short period beyond it if needed.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

notes: Postgraduate research programme (Civil Engineering PhD) in the Department of Architecture & Civil Engineering at the University of Bath; includes climate adaptation and environmental research.
